fieldGuide.physicalConstraint: 1=pure software, 5=hard physical monopoly with multi-year lead times
fieldGuide.constraintType: OPTIONAL, set for physicalConstraint>=4 only. ZERO WEIGHT — surfacing only, no gate reads it. WHICH KIND of physical constraint the score rests on, because the same pc=4 decays at very different rates. 'tech'=process/IP/lead-time know-how, broken by the next technology generation (endogenous, slow, visible in roadmaps). 'geo'=transport-radius economics, mineral rights, siting, grid interconnect or permitted capacity — broken by policy, permitting, tax incentive or new capacity coming online (EXOGENOUS and materially faster; the constraint is rented from a jurisdiction, not owned). 'regulatory'=license, approval, liability or defence contract. 'unclassified'=the pc score has no physical referent and is a metaphor (crypto network effects) — a flagged classification debt, NOT a fix. Purpose: a falsifiable posterior test — do geo-type pc>=4 names underperform tech-type ones? Absence on a pc>=4 ticker = not yet classified.
fieldGuide.aiContribution: 0.0-1.0, estimated % of forward revenue/earnings growth attributable to AI thesis
fieldGuide.layerRole: primary=core layer representative, secondary=partial exposure, bridge=spans multiple layers
fieldGuide.supplyChainEvidence: OPTIONAL array of {claim, source, type}. EXTERNAL proof the ticker actually occupies the chokepoint it is mapped to — patent cross-reference, teardown/BOM, regulatory filing, third-party report. type ∈ {patent|teardown|filing|thirdparty|contract}. NEVER company IR self-report or press release. Purpose: separate verified chain position from narrative. Absence = thesis rests on management's word.
fieldGuide.catalysts: OPTIONAL array of {date, event, source}. Concrete dated events backing timeToRealize (e.g. a named platform's mass-production quarter, a capacity-online date, a contract decision window). date in YYYY-MM or YYYY-Qn. Replaces vague near/mid/far with falsifiable timeline. A passed catalyst date with no thesis movement is itself a falsification signal.
fieldGuide.moatCapture: OPTIONAL 1-5. WHO captures the private-correctness moat (orthogonal to physicalConstraint, which covers PHYSICAL lead-time only). 1=pure supplier, the moat accrues to the incumbent above (component vendor) or the customer below; the ticker is a replaceable vendor (the 'sold to whoever has the most compute' trap). 3=contested/shared, capture undecided. 5=the ticker itself holds the private ground truth / license / liability / user habit that a smarter general model still cannot enter. Source: Sarah Guo 2026 moat thesis — 'moat exists' != 'startup captures it'. A physicalConstraint=1 ticker can be moatCapture=5 (e.g. a licensed, liability-bearing, workflow-embedded app). Absence = not yet assessed; funnel falls back to the physical gate alone.
fieldGuide.moatLocks: OPTIONAL array, subset of {licensing, liability, privateData, userHabit, integration}. The NON-physical locks backing moatCapture. Physical lead-time is NOT listed here — it lives in physicalConstraint, do not double-count. Empty/absent with low moatCapture = supplier with no defensible lock.
fieldGuide.moatFalsification: OPTIONAL string. Falsifiable condition under which the moat is shown to accrue elsewhere or be absorbed by the model layer (e.g. 'a general model + public data replicates 80% of the function' or 'the incumbent in-houses it'). Same falsification discipline as thesisFalsification.
fieldGuide.falsificationObservations: OPTIONAL array, added v2.9.0. A declared falsifier is only worth its check date if someone records what the measurement actually said when the date arrived — otherwise a signal that has been tested and survived is indistinguishable from one nobody looked at, and both quietly read as 'thesis intact'. Each entry states which falsifier it targets, the measured value, the declared threshold, the verdict (TRIGGERED / NOT TRIGGERED / INCONCLUSIVE), and its source. Two rules: (1) record the observation whether or not it fires — a non-firing observation is the more common and more easily lost one; (2) if the observation contradicts something previously written here, the entry carries an explicit `correction` field rather than the earlier text being edited away. Price action is recorded under `priceContext` and is deliberately kept separate from the measurement — a stock falling is not evidence that a falsifier fired.
fieldGuide.thesisFalsification: Falsification conditions for the ticker thesis. Appending a falsifier is preferred to editing one: a threshold that measurement shows to be gameable stays in the list as written so the original judgement remains auditable, and the refinement enters as a new numbered entry (see INTC #6 vs #2, GLW #7 vs #6).

funnelPassCriteria.defensibility: physicalConstraint>=4 OR moatCapture>=4 (survives commoditization via a PHYSICAL chokepoint OR a non-physical moat — either suffices)
funnelPassCriteria.supplierTrapWarning: moatCapture<=2 flags a supplier-trap (moat accrues upstream/downstream) — WARNING only, not an auto-fail

falsificationObservations.threshold: #2: "On-device AI fails to reach commercial tipping point — <10% of enterprise apps deploy edge inference by 2026"
falsificationObservations.result: CANNOT BE EVALUATED — and that is the finding, not an excuse. The deadline written into the falsifier has arrived and no check occurred, because the quantity it names is not published by anyone. There is no source for "share of enterprise apps deploying edge inference". A falsifier whose measurement does not exist cannot fire, cannot be refuted, and silently converts a position into an article of faith while appearing to be disciplined. #1 (Apple Silicon perf-per-watt lead) has the same defect in weaker form — no standard on-device AI benchmark is named. #3 (loses the Apple modem contract) is genuinely measurable and is NOT triggered.
falsificationObservations.thresholdDefect: Two distinct failure modes now recorded in this repo. INTC #2 and CRCL #2 were GAMEABLE — measurable but reachable by means that do not validate the thesis. QCOM #2 is UNMEASURABLE — no data source exists at any price. The second is worse: a gameable threshold at least produces a number to argue about. Per the append-don't-edit rule #2 stands as written and successor #4 is added with a measurement drawn from the company's own segment disclosure.
falsificationObservations.crowdingReading: HANDLE WITH CARE, and the care is quantitative. UBS's "extreme short crowding" is a proprietary positioning factor, not short interest. The observable short interest is 3.84% of float — against MU's 3.21%, a name in the same note's EXTREME LONG cohort. On the public measure the two are close, so the nine-year claim cannot be verified from outside UBS and is recorded as reported, not as fact. Separately, contrarian positioning is not a thesis: this book already rejected buying a name because it was hated (framework line 235 on sell-side and KOL narrative). The datum earns a place here only because it points the opposite way from the engine, and disagreement between an independent measure and the engine is what this file is for.
falsificationObservations.theCheapnessQuestion: The engine calls QCOM the cheapest active holding after NVDA. The fundamentals say revenue is SHRINKING 3.5% year over year. Those are consistent, and the consistency is the whole point: a forward P/E of 14.5 on declining revenue is not obviously cheap, it is a price for decline. Note the structural exposure this creates in the funnel: aiContribution is set at 0.45 and is defined as a share of FORWARD REVENUE GROWTH. If forward growth is near zero or negative, 45% of it is not a meaningful gate — the denominator problem GOVERNANCE flagged in v2.8.0 section 2 has its sharpest instance here, in the cheapest name in the book. Flagged, not repriced.
falsificationObservations.conclusion: No rating moved. physicalConstraint HELD at 3, moatCapture HELD at 4, aiContribution HELD at 0.45 — none was audited against evidence in this review and none should move on a positioning datum. Per v2.9.5, QCOM is a LICENSOR (its moatFalsification names "the licensing stream" as revenue it collects), so the queue-vs-chokepoint test does not apply to it; its correct falsifier is substitution, which #3 already carries. TWO THINGS THIS REVIEW CHANGES: falsifier #2 is now on record as unmeasurable rather than untriggered, and successor #4 gives the position a test that can actually be run against a filing. Also noted for later: constraintType is undefined on this ticker while physicalConstraint is 3 — not fixed here.
falsificationObservations.confidence: HIGH on engine output and fetched fundamentals. HIGH on the judgement that #2 is unmeasurable — the claim is that no public source exists, and if one is produced this entry should be revised. MEDIUM on the UBS crowding figures (Chinese-language secondary summary; the proprietary factor cannot be checked). LOW on any read of what the crowding implies for forward return — none is asserted.
